The SJ RF150 is a 150 HP industrial fixed-speed rotary screw air compressor engineered for large-scale compressed air installations requiring elevated operating pressure and substantial airflow.

With a motor rating of 110 kW and rated air delivery of 516 CFM (14.61 m³/min) at 13 bar, this model is designed for evaluating high-demand compressed air systems across heavy engineering, industrial surface preparation, mining support, large pneumatic installations and specialized manufacturing operations.

At this capacity, compressor selection becomes closely connected to the overall production system. Air consumption, simultaneous equipment operation, pressure losses, compressed air quality and operating hours must all be considered when designing the installation.

The SJ RF150 combines fixed-speed rotary screw compression technology with a 13 bar pressure configuration for industrial processes that genuinely require higher compressed air pressure.

PRODUCT CONFIGURATION

Model: SJ RF150
Motor Power: 150 HP
Motor Rating: 110 kW
Operating Pressure: 13 bar(g)
Pressure Equivalent: 190 PSI(g)
Rated Air Delivery: 516 CFM
Air Delivery: 14.61 m³/min
Compression Technology: Single Stage Rotary Screw
Operating Technology: Fixed Speed


WHY CHOOSE THIS CAPACITY?

A 150 HP compressor is generally evaluated when an industrial facility has a substantial and relatively consistent compressed air requirement.

The SJ RF150 provides 516 CFM at 13 bar, making it relevant for larger installations where several pneumatic processes operate simultaneously or where individual machines have high compressed air consumption.

This capacity can be considered for:

• Large abrasive blasting and surface preparation facilities.
• Multiple high-consumption pneumatic equipment stations.
• Heavy engineering and steel fabrication plants.
• Mining and quarrying support installations.
• Industrial pneumatic conveying systems.
• Specialized high-pressure production machinery.
• Large centralized compressed air distribution networks.

The 150 HP rating should not be used as the sole basis for compressor selection.

A proper assessment should establish the total connected airflow demand, actual simultaneous consumption, required pressure at each machine and pressure losses across the complete compressed air network.

For applications that require 13 bar at the point of use, the compressor discharge pressure must also account for losses through the air treatment equipment, receiver connections, piping and distribution components.

A compressor with higher nominal horsepower does not automatically guarantee sufficient pressure or airflow at every connected machine.


ADVANCED ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RF150 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology for industrial compressed air generation.

Rotary screw compressors operate through the interaction of two precision-engineered screw rotors inside a compression element. Air enters through the intake system, becomes trapped between the rotor profiles and casing, and is compressed as the air volume reduces during rotor rotation.

The compressed air then moves towards the discharge side of the compression element.

The rotary screw arrangement is particularly relevant to industrial installations requiring substantial airflow and sustained compressed air availability.

Important functional aspects include:

• ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION ELEMENT: Generates compressed air through the rotating screw rotor arrangement.
• AIR INTAKE SYSTEM: Supplies incoming atmospheric air to the compression element.
• LUBRICATION SYSTEM: Supports lubrication and thermal management in oil-injected configurations.
• AIR-OIL SEPARATION: Separates compressor oil from compressed air in oil-injected configurations.
• COOLING ARRANGEMENT: Manages heat generated during compression.
• DISCHARGE SYSTEM: Transfers compressed air towards the downstream installation.

The complete compressor configuration should be evaluated according to its technical documentation and the actual supplied equipment.

For a 150 HP installation, the condition of the intake filter, lubrication system, separator element and cooling surfaces becomes particularly important because maintenance deficiencies can affect operating temperature, pressure stability and machine availability.


FIXED SPEED OPERATING TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RF150 is a fixed-speed rotary screw compressor.

Its motor operates at its designated speed during loaded operation. Compressor capacity is generally managed through load/unload control according to the configured pressure settings.

During loaded operation, the compressor supplies compressed air to the connected system. When system pressure reaches the configured unloading threshold, the controller changes the compressor operating state according to its control arrangement.

When pressure falls to the configured loading threshold, the compressor returns to loaded operation.

This operating arrangement is commonly used in industrial facilities with relatively stable compressed air demand.

KEY OPERATING CHARACTERISTICS:

• Fixed motor speed during loaded operation.
• Load/unload-based capacity regulation.
• Suitable for evaluating sustained industrial air demand.
• Operating pressure managed through configured control settings.
• No continuous motor-speed modulation as in a VFD compressor.

ENERGY AND OPERATING CONSIDERATIONS:

A fixed-speed compressor should be selected with reference to the actual plant air-demand profile.

If compressed air consumption fluctuates significantly, frequent loading and unloading or extended unloaded operation may affect overall energy performance.

The compressor's electricity consumption depends on actual operating conditions, loading pattern, discharge pressure, cooling conditions and maintenance condition.

For a 150 HP machine, unnecessary pressure increases can result in substantial additional electrical consumption over long operating hours.

Therefore, 13 bar should be selected only where the connected machinery or production process genuinely requires this pressure. Where equipment operates at a lower pressure, the complete system should be assessed for the possibility of using a lower-pressure configuration.


PREMIUM INDUSTRIAL COMPONENTS & ENGINEERING CONFIGURATION

A 150 HP industrial screw compressor requires coordinated engineering across its compression element, motor, lubrication, cooling, separation and electrical systems.

The SJ RF150 configuration can be evaluated around the following major functional assemblies:

1. ROTARY SCREW AIR END

The compression element is the central assembly responsible for generating compressed air.

Its rotor geometry, operating speed, lubrication arrangement and thermal operating limits influence compressor performance.

Air-end selection should be confirmed against the specified 150 HP and 13 bar operating configuration.

2. INDUSTRIAL ELECTRIC MOTOR

The compressor has a 150 HP / 110 kW motor rating.

Motor selection and installation should account for rated voltage, frequency, current, insulation class, protection rating, starting method and operating environment.

Motor efficiency and enclosure specifications should be verified from the actual motor datasheet rather than assumed from the compressor horsepower.

3. AIR INTAKE FILTRATION

The intake filtration system removes airborne particulate matter before air enters the compression element.

In dusty industrial environments, filter condition and replacement intervals require particular attention.

A restricted intake filter can affect compressor operation and increase maintenance requirements.

4. LUBRICATION AND OIL FILTRATION

For oil-injected configurations, compressor oil supports lubrication, cooling and sealing functions within the compression system.

The oil filter helps remove contaminants from circulating lubricant and protects critical components.

Oil type, oil quantity, filtration arrangement and replacement intervals should follow the supplied compressor manufacturer's instructions.

5. AIR-OIL SEPARATOR ELEMENT

The separator system reduces the amount of oil carried over with compressed air in oil-injected screw compressor configurations.

Separator condition is important for maintaining compressed air quality and avoiding abnormal oil carryover.

The correct separator element must be selected according to the supplied compressor configuration.

6. INDUSTRIAL COOLING ASSEMBLY

The cooling arrangement manages heat generated during compression and supports the operating temperature requirements of the compressor.

Oil cooling and compressed air aftercooling functions should be considered according to the actual machine design.

7. ELECTRICAL CONTROL PANEL

The electrical control arrangement manages compressor operation and provides configured protection and monitoring functions.

Controller type, protection settings, sensors and electrical components should be confirmed in the approved technical configuration.

8. INDUSTRIAL ENCLOSURE AND SERVICE ACCESS

The enclosure and internal equipment arrangement should provide suitable access for inspection, routine maintenance and service activities.

For large-capacity compressors, sufficient machine-room space and ventilation are important installation requirements.

COMPONENT CONFIGURATION NOTE:

Actual component brands, motor specifications, controller model, drive arrangement, cooling configuration and included accessories should be confirmed in the approved technical quotation. No specific component brand or optional feature should be assumed unless it is listed in the supplied configuration.

HEAVY DUTY COOLING SYSTEM

The SJ RF150 is a 150 HP industrial screw compressor designed for high-capacity compressed air generation at 13 bar pressure.

At this power level, effective heat management is essential for maintaining the operating condition of the compression element, lubrication system, motor and associated assemblies.

The cooling arrangement manages heat generated during compression through the compressor's cooling system.

Its functional cooling elements may include:

• OIL COOLER: Removes heat from circulating compressor oil in oil-injected configurations.
• COOLING FAN: Supports heat rejection through the cooler assembly.
• COOLING AIRFLOW: Directs ambient air across the heat-exchange surfaces.
• AFTERCOOLER: Where included, reduces compressed air temperature before downstream moisture separation.

For a 150 HP installation, machine-room ventilation requires particular attention.

INSTALLATION CONSIDERATIONS:

• Provide adequate clearance around the compressor.
• Ensure unrestricted cooling-air intake and discharge.
• Avoid recirculation of hot discharge air into the compressor intake.
• Maintain clean cooler surfaces and ventilation passages.
• Keep ambient temperature within the manufacturer's specified operating limits.
• Provide sufficient space for inspection and maintenance.

Inadequate ventilation, dust accumulation and high ambient temperatures can contribute to elevated operating temperatures and reduced equipment reliability.

The cooling system should be inspected and maintained according to the manufacturer's service instructions.


INTELLIGENT ELECTRICAL & SAFETY FEATURES

The SJ RF150 has a 150 HP / 110 kW motor rating. Its electrical infrastructure must be appropriately engineered for the motor's electrical characteristics and the installation environment.

Functional control and protection provisions may include:

• MOTOR STARTING AND STOPPING: Controls compressor operation through the electrical system.
• LOAD/UNLOAD CONTROL: Regulates compressor loading according to configured system pressure.
• PRESSURE MONITORING: Supports monitoring of operating pressure and configured pressure limits.
• TEMPERATURE PROTECTION: Helps protect the compressor against abnormal operating temperatures.
• MOTOR PROTECTION: Electrical protection is selected according to the motor rating and panel design.
• FAULT INDICATION: Controller indications assist maintenance personnel in identifying abnormal operating conditions.
• EMERGENCY STOP: Provides an emergency shutdown function where fitted in the supplied configuration.

ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS:

• Verify motor rated current and starting characteristics.
• Select cables according to current capacity and installation conditions.
• Evaluate voltage drop across the electrical supply.
• Provide suitable overload and short-circuit protection.
• Ensure proper electrical earthing.
• Verify incoming supply voltage and frequency.
• Follow applicable industrial electrical safety standards.

Controller model, sensor arrangement, protection settings, alarm functions and emergency-stop configuration should be confirmed against the actual machine supplied.

Electrical installation and commissioning should be carried out by qualified personnel.


STANDARD FEATURES

The SJ RF150 is a fixed-speed, single-stage rotary screw compressor designed for large industrial compressed air installations.

Its core functional systems include:

• 150 HP / 110 kW motor rating.
• Single-stage rotary screw compression technology.
• Fixed-speed operating arrangement.
• Air intake filtration system.
• Compressor lubrication arrangement, subject to supplied design.
• Oil filtration system for oil-injected configurations.
• Air-oil separation arrangement.
• Industrial cooling system.
• Electrical control and protection arrangement.
• Pressure monitoring and load/unload control, subject to controller configuration.
• Industrial enclosure and ventilation arrangement, as supplied.
• Service access for routine inspection and maintenance.

The exact standard equipment, component brands, motor efficiency class, controller functions and machine configuration should be confirmed in the approved technical quotation.


OPTIONAL FEATURES & COMPRESSED AIR SYSTEM ACCESSORIES

The SJ RF150 produces 516 CFM (14.61 m³/min) at 13 bar.

At this airflow level, the downstream compressed air treatment and distribution system must be sized carefully. An undersized dryer, filter, separator or pipeline can introduce excessive pressure drop and restrict the airflow available to production equipment.

The following accessories can be incorporated according to the application requirements.

1. INDUSTRIAL AIR RECEIVER TANK

An air receiver stores compressed air and helps manage short-duration demand fluctuations.

For a 150 HP compressor, receiver capacity should be calculated using:

• Compressor delivery.
• Peak compressed air demand.
• Permissible pressure variation.
• Compressor load/unload control strategy.
• Required reserve capacity.

The receiver must have an appropriate design pressure, certified construction and suitable safety accessories for the installation.

2. REFRIGERATED AIR DRYER

A refrigerated air dryer reduces compressed air moisture by cooling the air and removing condensed water.

It is suitable for evaluating general industrial compressed air systems where the required pressure dew point is compatible with refrigerated drying technology.

The dryer should be selected according to:

• Actual inlet airflow.
• Maximum operating pressure.
• Inlet air temperature.
• Ambient temperature.
• Required pressure dew point.
• Manufacturer's capacity correction factors.

A nominal 500 CFM dryer should not automatically be assumed suitable for a 516 CFM compressor installation without checking its corrected capacity under actual operating conditions.

3. DESICCANT AIR DRYER

A desiccant air dryer can be considered when a lower pressure dew point is required.

Potential applications include moisture-sensitive manufacturing, specialized pneumatic equipment and industrial processes requiring dry compressed air.

Selection should account for required dew point, purge-air consumption, operating pressure and total lifecycle energy cost.

4. MOISTURE SEPARATOR

A moisture separator removes bulk liquid condensate from compressed air, generally after cooling.

It helps reduce liquid water entering downstream dryers and filtration equipment.

For high-flow installations, separator capacity and allowable pressure drop must be checked against the actual operating conditions.

5. PRE-FILTER AND AFTER-FILTER

Industrial compressed air filters remove contaminants according to their filtration grade.

A suitable filtration arrangement can be selected for:

• Particulate removal.
• Liquid water and oil aerosol reduction.
• Protection of downstream air treatment equipment.
• Improved compressed air quality for connected machinery.

Filter flow capacity and pressure rating should be suitable for the 516 CFM, 13 bar configuration.

6. MICRO-FILTER

A micro-filter provides finer filtration where lower oil-aerosol and particulate levels are required.

Its filtration performance should be selected according to the required outlet air quality and specified filtration efficiency.

7. ACTIVATED CARBON FILTER

An activated carbon filter can be considered where reduction of oil vapour and odour is required.

It should be installed with suitable upstream filtration. It is not a replacement for proper moisture removal or other filtration stages.

8. AUTOMATIC CONDENSATE DRAIN

Automatic drains can be installed on air receivers, moisture separators, filters and dryers.

They help remove accumulated liquid condensate and reduce dependence on manual drainage.

Drain capacity and pressure rating should be appropriate for the installation.

9. OIL-WATER SEPARATOR

An oil-water separator can be incorporated to treat oil-contaminated condensate before disposal, subject to applicable environmental and wastewater regulations.

10. PRESSURE REGULATING VALVE

A pressure regulator can reduce downstream pressure where connected machinery requires less than 13 bar.

The regulator must be selected according to required airflow, inlet pressure, outlet pressure and allowable pressure drop.

Pressure regulation does not increase the available compressor airflow.

11. INDUSTRIAL COMPRESSED AIR PIPING

A 516 CFM compressed air installation requires an appropriately engineered distribution network.

Piping design should consider:

• Required flow rate.
• Operating pressure.
• Pipeline diameter.
• Total pipeline length.
• Fittings and branch connections.
• Simultaneous equipment demand.
• Allowable pressure drop.
• Future expansion requirements.

Industrial aluminium compressed air piping or another suitably engineered piping system can be selected according to installation requirements.

12. AIR QUALITY AND SYSTEM MONITORING

Additional monitoring equipment can be incorporated where process requirements justify it:

• Airflow meters for compressed air consumption monitoring.
• Dew point monitors for moisture control.
• Differential pressure indicators across filters.
• Pressure gauges at the receiver and critical distribution points.
• Energy monitoring for compressor electrical consumption.

IMPORTANT 13 BAR INSTALLATION REQUIREMENT:

All downstream equipment must be suitable for the maximum applicable operating pressure.

This includes:

• Air receiver tanks.
• Air dryers.
• Moisture separators.
• Pre-filters and after-filters.
• Micro-filters and activated carbon filters.
• Pressure regulators.
• Automatic drain valves.
• Compressed air piping and fittings.
• Hoses, couplings and safety devices.

Components designed only for conventional 7–10 bar systems must not automatically be used in a 13 bar installation.


TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

Product: SJ RF150 Fixed Speed Screw Air Compressor

Model: SJ RF150
Motor Power: 150 HP
Motor Rating: 110 kW
Maximum Operating Pressure: 13 bar(g)
Pressure Equivalent: 190 PSI(g)
Pressure Equivalent: 1.3 MPa(g)
Air Delivery at 13 Bar: 516 CFM
Air Delivery at 13 Bar: 14.61 m³/min
Compressor Technology: Rotary Screw
Compression Configuration: Single Stage
Operating Technology: Fixed Speed

PRESSURE-WISE AIR DELIVERY:

At 8 bar:
717 CFM / 20.31 m³/min

At 10 bar:
600 CFM / 16.99 m³/min

At 13 bar:
516 CFM / 14.61 m³/min

These are the official airflow capacities at their respective operating pressure configurations.

For the 13 bar SJ RF150 product configuration, use 516 CFM / 14.61 m³/min as the rated airflow.

Final electrical, dimensional, connection, noise and component details should be confirmed through the approved technical datasheet for the supplied configuration.


INDUSTRIAL APPLICATIONS

The SJ RF150 150 HP 13 Bar Screw Air Compressor can be evaluated for large industrial installations requiring elevated compressed air pressure and substantial airflow.

With 516 CFM (14.61 m³/min) at 13 bar, it offers a higher rated airflow capacity than the SJ RF120, making it relevant for evaluating larger production systems and multiple high-consumption pneumatic equipment stations.

Its application suitability depends on the actual pressure and airflow requirements of the connected machinery.

1. LARGE ABRASIVE BLASTING & INDUSTRIAL SURFACE PREPARATION

Potential applications include:

• Large industrial blast rooms.
• Multiple pressure blast pot installations.
• Multi-nozzle abrasive blasting systems.
• Shipyard surface preparation facilities.
• Steel structure blasting installations.
• Heavy fabrication surface cleaning.
• Industrial shot-blasting equipment with pneumatic requirements.
• Large-scale rust and coating removal operations.

The RF150 can be evaluated for larger blasting installations where several blasting points operate simultaneously.

However, actual suitability depends on nozzle diameter, abrasive type, blasting pressure, hose dimensions and simultaneous air consumption.

The combined airflow demand must remain within the available 516 CFM at the required pressure.

2. MINING, QUARRYING & DRILLING SUPPORT SYSTEMS

Potential applications include:

• Pneumatic rock drilling equipment.
• Quarry drilling machinery.
• Industrial pneumatic scaling equipment.
• Mining maintenance stations.
• Pneumatic drilling support systems.
• Heavy-duty pneumatic tools.
• Specialized compressed air distribution for mining equipment.

Some mining and down-the-hole drilling systems require airflow substantially beyond 516 CFM or operate at different pressure specifications.

The drilling equipment manufacturer's pressure, airflow and duty-cycle requirements must be verified before confirming compressor suitability.

3. HEAVY STEEL FABRICATION & METAL PROCESSING

Potential applications include:

• Large steel fabrication facilities.
• Industrial abrasive surface preparation.
• Heavy engineering maintenance equipment.
• Pneumatic clamping and specialized fixtures where specified.
• Dedicated high-pressure pneumatic machinery.
• Large industrial air-blowing stations.
• Specialized production equipment requiring elevated compressed air pressure.

Conventional CNC and VMC machines generally operate at lower compressed air pressures. A 13 bar compressor should only be selected where a specific machine or connected process genuinely requires elevated pressure.

4. LARGE-SCALE CONSTRUCTION & INFRASTRUCTURE EQUIPMENT

Potential applications include:

• Heavy-duty pneumatic breakers.
• Industrial jackhammer installations.
• Pneumatic demolition equipment.
• Multiple construction-site pneumatic tool stations.
• Infrastructure maintenance machinery.
• Specialized civil engineering equipment.
• Large centralized pneumatic service systems.

For installations involving multiple pneumatic tools, the combined air consumption and operating sequence must be calculated.

Long hoses and distribution pipelines can introduce pressure losses that affect equipment performance.

5. INDUSTRIAL PNEUMATIC CONVEYING & BULK MATERIAL HANDLING

Potential applications include:

• Pressure-based pneumatic conveying systems.
• Specialized powder transfer installations.
• Bulk material handling equipment.
• Industrial raw material transfer systems.
• Dedicated high-pressure conveying machinery.
• Process-industry material movement systems.
• Pneumatic transfer equipment for compatible dry materials.

Conveying-system requirements depend on material density, particle characteristics, pipeline diameter, conveying distance, transfer rate and pressure regime.

Dense-phase and dilute-phase conveying systems have different operating characteristics. Compressor selection must follow the conveying-system supplier's engineering calculations.

6. LARGE INDUSTRIAL PLANTS & CENTRALIZED COMPRESSED AIR NETWORKS

Potential applications include:

• Centralized industrial compressed air stations.
• Multiple high-consumption pneumatic production lines.
• Large industrial maintenance facilities.
• Specialized high-pressure manufacturing processes.
• Dedicated compressed air supply for heavy machinery.
• Multiple pneumatic equipment zones.
• Industrial compressed air distribution networks.

The RF150 can be considered where the combined air demand remains within its rated delivery and the connected equipment requires the available operating pressure.

APPLICATION ENGINEERING NOTE:

A 150 HP compressor should not be selected solely on the basis of plant size or the number of connected machines.

A technically correct selection requires:

• Total connected air consumption.
• Simultaneous operating demand.
• Required pressure at each machine.
• Pressure losses through dryers, filters and piping.
• Compressed air leakage.
• Peak demand and consumption fluctuations.
• Required compressed air quality.
• Operating hours and duty profile.

The available airflow must be sufficient at the required pressure after accounting for downstream system losses.

Compressed air pipeline or equipment pressure testing also requires a separate engineering safety assessment. This compressor should not automatically be considered suitable for pressure-vessel proof testing or hydraulic testing applications.


FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q1. What is the air delivery of the SJ RF150 150 HP compressor at 13 bar?

The SJ RF150 delivers 516 CFM (14.61 m³/min) at 13 bar according to the official specification sheet.

Q2. What is the motor power of the SJ RF150?

The SJ RF150 has a 150 HP motor rating, equivalent to 110 kW.

Q3. What type of compressor is the SJ RF150?

It is a single-stage, fixed-speed rotary screw air compressor designed for industrial compressed air applications.

Q4. Is the SJ RF150 suitable for large abrasive blasting installations?

It can be evaluated for large blasting facilities and multiple blasting points, provided their combined airflow demand remains within 516 CFM at the required pressure.

Q5. Can this compressor supply multiple industrial machines simultaneously?

Yes, provided the combined air consumption of the operating machines remains within the compressor's available airflow at the required pressure. Simultaneous demand, pressure losses and equipment operating cycles must be considered.

Q6. What is the airflow difference between the 8 bar, 10 bar and 13 bar configurations?

The official SJ RF150 airflow specifications are:

• 8 bar: 717 CFM / 20.31 m³/min.
• 10 bar: 600 CFM / 16.99 m³/min.
• 13 bar: 516 CFM / 14.61 m³/min.

The higher-pressure configuration provides lower airflow than the lower-pressure configurations.

Q7. Can the SJ RF150 be connected to an air receiver tank and industrial air dryer?

Yes. A suitably sized pressure-rated air receiver and compatible air dryer can be integrated into the system. Their flow capacity, pressure rating and operating conditions must be suitable for the 516 CFM, 13 bar installation.

Q8. Is the SJ RF150 suitable for mining and quarry drilling?

It can be considered for compatible pneumatic drilling and mining support equipment. Large drilling systems, particularly high-consumption DTH equipment, may require airflow beyond the compressor's rated capacity. OEM specifications must be checked.

Q9. Can the 13 bar compressor supply machinery requiring 7 or 8 bar?

Yes. A correctly sized pressure regulator can reduce downstream pressure to the machinery's required operating level. However, operating at unnecessarily high pressure can increase energy consumption, so the complete system pressure should be optimized.

Q10. What is the difference between the SJ RF120 and SJ RF150 at 13 bar?

Their official specifications are:

• SJ RF120: 120 HP / 90 kW, 434 CFM / 12.29 m³/min.
• SJ RF150: 150 HP / 110 kW, 516 CFM / 14.61 m³/min.

The RF150 provides approximately 18.9% higher rated airflow at 13 bar.

Q11. Can the SJ RF150 operate continuously in an industrial facility?

Rotary screw compressors are commonly used in industrial systems with sustained compressed air demand. Actual operating duty, ambient conditions, service intervals and permissible operating limits must follow the supplied machine's technical documentation.

Q12. How should the air dryer and filtration system be selected for this compressor?

The dryer and filters should be selected according to actual airflow, operating pressure, inlet temperature, ambient conditions, required pressure dew point and filtration grade.

For the RF150, the rated airflow reference is 516 CFM at 13 bar. Corrected equipment capacity should be checked under actual operating conditions.


WHY CHOOSE SARV JAGAT?

Sarv Jagat Corporation provides industrial compressed air solutions covering screw compressors, reciprocating compressors, air dryers, air receiver tanks, filtration systems, spare parts and compressor servicing.

The SJ RF150 belongs to the SJ R Series and is designed for industrial users evaluating a 150 HP fixed-speed rotary screw compressor with a 13 bar operating pressure configuration.

Its rated delivery of 516 CFM (14.61 m³/min) makes it relevant for evaluating larger compressed air installations involving abrasive blasting, heavy engineering, mining support, bulk material handling and specialized pneumatic machinery.

The complete compressed air system can be configured around the actual production requirements, including:

• Industrial screw compressor selection.
• Air receiver tank sizing.
• Refrigerated and desiccant air dryer selection.
• Moisture separation and compressed air filtration.
• Pressure-rated distribution piping.
• Compressed air system monitoring.
• Spare parts and maintenance requirements.

For large industrial applications, correct compressor selection depends on the relationship between pressure, airflow, air quality and operating demand.

The SJ RF150 provides 516 CFM at 13 bar and should be evaluated against the actual requirements of the connected equipment.

At this capacity, compressor selection involves more than matching motor horsepower to machinery. The complete compressed air system must be evaluated, including simultaneous air consumption, pressure stability, downstream treatment capacity, distribution losses and operating duty.

The SJ RF175 combines single-stage rotary screw compression technology with a fixed-speed operating arrangement and a 13 bar pressure configuration.

It is particularly relevant for facilities where a substantial volume of compressed air must be delivered at elevated pressure to compatible industrial equipment.

PRODUCT CONFIGURATION

Model: SJ RF175
Motor Power: 175 HP
Motor Rating: 132 kW
Operating Pressure: 13 bar(g)
Pressure Equivalent: 190 PSI(g)

WHY CHOOSE THIS CAPACITY?

The 175 HP capacity is intended for evaluating large industrial compressed air requirements where smaller compressor configurations may not provide sufficient airflow for the combined operating demand.

The SJ RF175 delivers 636 CFM at 13 bar, making it relevant to installations involving several high-consumption pneumatic processes or large individual equipment systems.

• Large multi-nozzle abrasive blasting facilities.

• Mining and quarrying pneumatic equipment.
• Large pneumatic conveying installations.
• Centralized high-pressure compressed air networks.

Selecting a 13 bar compressor for equipment that operates at conventional lower pressures may increase energy consumption without providing a production benefit. The pressure requirement should therefore be established from the machinery manufacturer's specifications.


ADVANCED ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RF175 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology for industrial compressed air generation.

The compression element operates through the interaction of two precision-engineered screw rotors rotating inside a compression housing.

Atmospheric air enters through the intake system and becomes trapped between the rotor profiles and casing. As the rotors turn, the trapped air moves along the compression chamber while its available volume decreases, resulting in an increase in air pressure.

The compressed air then moves towards the discharge side of the compression element.

This technology is widely used in industrial compressed air systems requiring substantial airflow and sustained air availability.

The main functional assemblies include:

• ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION ELEMENT: Generates compressed air through the rotating screw rotor arrangement.
• AIR INTAKE SYSTEM: Supplies incoming atmospheric air to the compression element.
• LUBRICATION SYSTEM: Supports lubrication and thermal management in oil-injected configurations.
• AIR-OIL SEPARATION SYSTEM: Separates compressor oil from compressed air in oil-injected configurations.
• COOLING ARRANGEMENT: Manages heat generated during compression.
• DISCHARGE SYSTEM: Transfers compressed air towards the downstream installation.

The condition and suitability of these assemblies influence compressor operation, maintenance requirements and long-term reliability.

For a 175 HP compressor, particular attention should be given to intake filtration, lubrication condition, separator performance and cooling-system maintenance.

The exact compression element design, lubrication arrangement and supplied component configuration should be confirmed from the machine's approved technical documentation.


FIXED SPEED OPERATING TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RF175 is a fixed-speed rotary screw air compressor.

During loaded operation, its motor runs at its designated operating speed. Compressor capacity is generally managed through a load/unload control arrangement according to the configured system pressure.

The operating sequence typically involves two main conditions:

LOADED OPERATION

When system pressure falls to the configured loading threshold, the compressor enters its loaded condition and supplies compressed air to the connected system.

UNLOADED OPERATION

When system pressure reaches the configured unloading threshold, the compressor changes its operating condition according to the controller and unloading arrangement.

This operating principle is commonly used in industrial facilities with relatively stable compressed air consumption.

KEY OPERATING CHARACTERISTICS:

• Fixed motor speed during loaded operation.
• Load/unload-based capacity regulation.
• Suitable for evaluating sustained industrial air demand.
• Operating pressure managed through configured control settings.

ENERGY AND OPERATING CONSIDERATIONS

The energy performance of a fixed-speed compressor depends on the actual air-demand profile and operating conditions.

In installations with highly fluctuating compressed air consumption, frequent loading and unloading or extended unloaded operation can affect overall energy efficiency.

For a 175 HP compressor, the electrical operating cost is an important part of the total ownership cost.

The following factors should be evaluated:

• Actual loaded and unloaded operating hours.
• Required discharge pressure.
• Leakage within the compressed air network.
• Intake filter and cooler condition.
• Pressure losses across downstream equipment.
• Air consumption during production and non-production periods.

ADVANCED ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV10 uses rotary screw compression technology, in which two intermeshing helical rotors compress air through a continuous compression process.

Unlike reciprocating compressors that use piston movement inside cylinders, rotary screw compressors generate compressed air through the rotation of precision-machined screw elements.

The compression process involves:

1. Air Intake:
Ambient air enters through the compressor intake system, where an intake filter helps restrict dust and airborne particles from entering the compression element.

2. Air Compression:
The screw rotors progressively reduce the volume of trapped air as it moves through the compression chamber.

3. Lubrication and Internal Cooling:
In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil performs lubrication, sealing and heat-removal functions within the compression element.

4. Oil-Air Separation:
The compressed air and oil mixture passes through the separation system, where oil is separated from the compressed-air stream.

5. Cooling:
The compressed air and circulating oil are cooled through their respective cooling arrangements, depending on the supplied configuration.

6. Compressed-Air Discharge:
The compressed air is delivered through the outlet system for storage, treatment and distribution to the connected pneumatic equipment.

Rotary screw technology is particularly relevant to industrial installations that require a continuous source of compressed air. Actual operating suitability depends on the compressor configuration, operating conditions, maintenance and application demand.

VARIABLE FREQUENCY DRIVE TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV10 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to regulate compressor motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

A conventional fixed-speed compressor generally operates at a fixed motor speed during loaded operation and regulates delivery through its control system. A VFD compressor can vary motor speed, allowing its air output to respond more closely to changing consumption.

How VFD operation works:

• Demand Monitoring:
The compressor control system monitors operating conditions and, where provided in the supplied configuration, compressed-air pressure feedback.

• Speed Regulation:
The VFD adjusts the electrical frequency supplied to the motor to regulate motor speed.

• Airflow Adjustment:
Changes in motor speed allow compressor output to increase or decrease within the permitted operating range.

• Pressure Regulation:
The control system manages compressor operation to maintain the configured pressure target, subject to the controller, pressure-sensing arrangement and system design.

• Reduced Unloaded Operation:
Under suitable operating conditions, variable-speed control can reduce the need for repeated loaded/unloaded operation associated with conventional fixed-speed control.

Potential advantages of VFD technology include:

• Better matching of compressor output to fluctuating air demand.
• Reduced unnecessary unloaded running under suitable operating conditions.
• More controlled pressure management when correctly configured.
• Potential improvement in operating efficiency for installations with variable consumption.
• Flexible integration into compressed-air systems with changing production requirements.

ADVANCED ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV20 uses rotary screw compression technology, where two intermeshing helical rotors compress air through a continuous compression process.

Unlike reciprocating compressors that use piston movement inside cylinders, rotary screw compressors generate compressed air through the rotation of precision-machined screw elements.

The compression process involves:

1. Air Intake:
Ambient air enters through the compressor intake system, where an intake filter helps restrict dust and airborne particles from entering the compression element.

2. Air Compression:
The screw rotors progressively reduce the volume of trapped air as it moves through the compression chamber.

3. Lubrication and Internal Cooling:
In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil performs lubrication, sealing and heat-removal functions within the compression element.

4. Oil-Air Separation:
The compressed air and oil mixture passes through the separation system, where oil is separated from the compressed-air stream.

5. Cooling:
The compressed air and circulating oil are cooled through their respective cooling arrangements, depending on the supplied configuration.

6. Compressed-Air Discharge:
The compressed air is delivered through the outlet system for storage, treatment and distribution to connected pneumatic equipment.

Rotary screw technology is relevant to industrial installations requiring a continuous source of compressed air. Actual operating suitability depends on machine configuration, operating conditions, maintenance and application demand.

VARIABLE FREQUENCY DRIVE TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV20 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to regulate compressor motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

A conventional fixed-speed compressor generally operates at a fixed motor speed during loaded operation and regulates delivery through its control system. A VFD compressor can vary motor speed to respond to changing air consumption.

How VFD operation works:

1. Demand Monitoring:
The compressor control system monitors operating conditions and, where provided in the supplied configuration, compressed-air pressure feedback.

2. Motor Speed Regulation:
The VFD adjusts the electrical frequency supplied to the motor to regulate motor speed.

3. Airflow Adjustment:
Changes in motor speed allow compressor output to increase or decrease within the permitted operating range.

4. Pressure Regulation:
The control system manages compressor operation against the configured pressure target, subject to the supplied controller and pressure-sensing arrangement.

5. Demand Matching:
Variable-speed operation can help align compressed-air production with changing consumption and reduce unnecessary unloaded running under suitable operating conditions.

Potential advantages of VFD technology include:

• Variable compressor output for changing production demand.
• More controlled pressure management when correctly configured.
• Reduced dependence on repeated loaded/unloaded operation in suitable applications.
• Potential reduction in energy consumption under appropriate variable-load conditions.
• Better integration with production systems having fluctuating pneumatic demand.

ENERGY PERFORMANCE AND VFD SELECTION

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of electricity savings.

Actual energy consumption depends on:

• Daily and seasonal compressed-air demand.

• Operating hours and load profile.
• Motor and compressor efficiency.
• Permitted motor-speed range.

For installations with stable and continuous air demand, a fixed-speed compressor may also be economically suitable. A VFD model should be evaluated against actual load data and lifecycle operating cost.

The compressor must operate within its specified minimum and maximum speed limits. Adequate cooling, lubrication and operating stability must be maintained throughout the permitted range.

ADVANCED ROTARY SCREW COMPRESSION TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV25 uses rotary screw compression technology, where two intermeshing helical rotors compress air through a continuous compression process.

Unlike reciprocating compressors that use piston movement inside cylinders, rotary screw compressors generate compressed air through the rotation of precision-machined screw elements.

The compression process involves:

1. Air Intake:
Ambient air enters through the compressor intake system, where an intake filter helps restrict dust and airborne particles from entering the compression element.

2. Air Compression:
The screw rotors progressively reduce the volume of trapped air as it moves through the compression chamber.

3. Lubrication and Internal Cooling:
In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil performs lubrication, sealing and heat-removal functions within the compression element.

4. Oil-Air Separation:
The compressed air and oil mixture passes through the separation system, where oil is separated from the compressed-air stream.

5. Cooling:
The compressed air and circulating oil are cooled through their respective cooling arrangements, depending on the supplied configuration.

6. Compressed-Air Discharge:
The compressed air is delivered through the outlet system for storage, treatment and distribution to connected pneumatic equipment.

Rotary screw technology is relevant to industrial installations requiring a continuous source of compressed air. Actual operating suitability depends on machine configuration, operating conditions, maintenance and application demand.

VARIABLE FREQUENCY DRIVE TECHNOLOGY

The SJ RV25 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to regulate compressor motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

A conventional fixed-speed compressor generally operates at a fixed motor speed during loaded operation and regulates delivery through its control system. A VFD compressor can vary motor speed to respond to changing air consumption.

How VFD operation works:

1. Demand Monitoring:
The compressor control system monitors operating conditions and, where provided in the supplied configuration, compressed-air pressure feedback.

2. Motor Speed Regulation:
The VFD adjusts the electrical frequency supplied to the motor to regulate motor speed.

3. Airflow Adjustment:
Changes in motor speed allow compressor output to increase or decrease within the permitted operating range.

4. Pressure Regulation:
The control system manages compressor operation against the configured pressure target, subject to the supplied controller and pressure-sensing arrangement.

5. Demand Matching:
Variable-speed operation can help align compressed-air production with changing consumption and reduce unnecessary unloaded running under suitable operating conditions.

Potential advantages of VFD technology include:

• Variable compressor output for changing production demand.
• More controlled pressure management when correctly configured.
• Reduced dependence on repeated loaded/unloaded operation in suitable applications.
• Potential reduction in energy consumption under appropriate variable-load conditions.
• Better integration with production systems having fluctuating pneumatic demand.

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV30 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. Rotary screw compressors operate through two intermeshing screw rotors that progressively reduce the volume of air trapped between the rotor profiles and the compressor housing.

The principal engineering functions of the rotary screw system include:

- Continuous rotary compression rather than reciprocating piston movement.

- Compression through the intermeshing rotor profiles.
- Lubrication and heat management in an oil-injected configuration, where supplied.

- Cooling and temperature management through the compressor package.

In a VFD compressor, the drive varies motor frequency and speed to adjust compressor output as system demand changes.

This can be useful in manufacturing facilities where air consumption changes due to:

- Intermittent pneumatic tool operation.
- Different production cycles.
- Multiple machines operating at varying loads.

**Reduced starting frequency:** Motor speed control can support controlled acceleration and reduce repeated direct-on-line starting, subject to drive configuration and operating logic.

**Variable-load suitability:** Particularly relevant where the plant's compressed-air consumption changes significantly during production.

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of electricity savings.

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV40 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. The compression process is based on two intermeshing screw rotors that progressively reduce the volume of air trapped between the rotor profiles and compressor housing.

During operation, atmospheric air enters through the intake arrangement and moves into the compression element. The rotating screw profiles transport and compress the air before it passes through the downstream separation and cooling arrangements, according to the supplied compressor configuration.

The principal functions of the rotary screw system include:

- Continuous rotary compression rather than reciprocating piston movement.
- Controlled atmospheric air intake through the filtration arrangement.
- Compression through intermeshing rotor profiles.
- Lubrication and heat management in an oil-injected configuration, where supplied.
- Air-oil separation before compressed air enters the downstream system.
- Thermal management through the compressor cooling arrangement.

## Variable Frequency Drive Technology

The SJ RV40 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to regulate motor speed according to changing compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

In a conventional fixed-speed compressor, the motor generally operates at a fixed speed during loaded operation, while capacity is regulated through its load/unload arrangement. A VFD compressor varies motor frequency and speed to adjust compressor output as system demand changes.

This can be useful in facilities where compressed-air consumption varies due to:

- Multiple production lines operating at different times.
- Intermittent abrasive blasting and pneumatic tool usage.
- Changing machine cycles.
- Batch-based manufacturing processes.
- Variable pneumatic demand from automated equipment.
- Different production schedules and shift patterns.
- Fluctuating demand from maintenance and utility stations.

**Pressure management:** Variable-speed control can help maintain the selected system pressure when the controller and installation are correctly configured.

**Reduced unnecessary unloading:** Under suitable operating conditions, VFD operation can reduce the time spent in conventional load/unload operation.

**Controlled motor acceleration:** The drive can provide controlled motor speed changes and reduce repeated direct-on-line starting, subject to the electrical configuration.

**Variable-load suitability:** Particularly relevant for production environments where air demand changes throughout the operating shift.

### Energy Consumption Considerations

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of electricity savings.

Actual energy performance depends on the plant's air-demand profile, pressure settings, leakage, operating hours, compressor operating range, motor efficiency, drive efficiency and system design.

A plant operating continuously near full compressor capacity may have limited energy-saving opportunity compared with a system experiencing substantial periods of reduced demand. An air-demand assessment and power-consumption analysis should therefore be completed before estimating financial savings.

4. Motor speed changes within the permitted operating range.

## Variable Frequency Drive Technology

The SJ RV60 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to adjust motor speed according to compressed-air demand within the designed operating range.

### How Variable-Speed Operation Works

1. Connected machines consume compressed air according to production activity.
2. The compressor control system monitors relevant operating parameters according to its configuration.
3. The VFD adjusts the electrical frequency supplied to the motor.
4. Motor speed changes within the permitted operating range.
5. Compressor output adjusts to the demand being served.

### Operational Advantages

- Variable-speed operation for fluctuating compressed-air demand

- Ambient temperature and cooling conditions

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV75 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. Rotary screw compressors operate through two intermeshing helical rotors that reduce the volume of trapped air as it moves through the compression chamber.

The principal functional stages include:

**Air Intake:** Atmospheric air enters through an intake filtration arrangement that helps prevent dust and particulate contamination from entering the compression system.

**Compression:** The rotating screw elements compress the incoming air as it travels through the rotor chamber.

**Lubrication and Thermal Management:** In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil supports lubrication, sealing and heat removal during compression.

**Air-Oil Separation:** The separation arrangement removes oil from the compressed-air stream in an oil-injected compressor configuration.

**Cooling:** The cooling arrangement manages operating temperatures of the compressor package and compressed air, according to the supplied configuration.

**Air Discharge:** Compressed air is delivered to the downstream system at the specified operating pressure and airflow conditions.

The rotary screw arrangement is suitable for industrial compressed-air applications requiring a continuous production utility, subject to the compressor's specified operating limits and maintenance requirements.

## Variable Frequency Drive Technology

The SJ RV75 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to adjust motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

In a variable-demand production facility, air consumption may change because of machine operating cycles, production shifts, equipment starting and stopping, or different departments operating simultaneously.

A VFD controls motor speed by varying the frequency of electrical power supplied to the motor. As demand changes, the compressor can adjust its output rather than relying only on conventional fixed-speed load/unload operation.

### Practical Benefits of VFD Operation

- Output can be adjusted to match changing air demand within the permitted speed range.
- Pressure regulation can be more responsive when the system is correctly configured.
- Reduced unloading periods may improve operating efficiency in suitable demand profiles.
- Variable-speed operation can reduce unnecessary start-stop cycling.
- The compressor can support industrial networks where compressed-air consumption changes during production.

### Important Energy Considerations

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of energy savings. Actual savings depend on:

- The plant's air-demand profile
- Compressor operating pressure
- Minimum and maximum permitted motor speed
- Leakage in the compressed-air network
- Operating hours and production shifts
- Compressor control settings
- Motor and drive efficiency
- The use of additional fixed-speed or variable-speed compressors

A VFD compressor is generally more beneficial where demand fluctuates over meaningful periods. In a plant operating continuously near maximum capacity, the potential energy advantage over a correctly selected fixed-speed compressor may be limited.

Higher operating pressure also generally increases compression energy consumption. Therefore, 13 bar should be selected only where the connected process genuinely requires it.

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV100 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. The compression mechanism consists of two intermeshing helical rotors that reduce the volume of trapped air as it moves through the compression chamber.

The principal functional stages include:

**Air Intake:** Atmospheric air enters through an intake filtration arrangement that helps prevent dust and particulate contamination from entering the compression system.

**Compression:** The rotating screw elements compress the incoming air as it travels through the rotor chamber.

**Lubrication and Thermal Management:** In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil supports lubrication, sealing and heat removal during compression.

**Air-Oil Separation:** The separation arrangement removes oil from the compressed-air stream in an oil-injected compressor configuration.

**Cooling:** The cooling arrangement manages operating temperatures of the compressor package and compressed air, according to the supplied configuration.

**Air Discharge:** Compressed air is delivered to the downstream system at the specified operating pressure and airflow conditions.

Rotary screw technology is widely used in industrial compressed-air systems requiring substantial air delivery, subject to the compressor's operating limits and maintenance requirements.

## Variable Frequency Drive Technology

The SJ RV100 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to adjust motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

Large manufacturing facilities rarely maintain identical compressed-air consumption throughout the day. Different production lines, pneumatic tools, blasting stations and maintenance activities can operate at different times, creating variations in total demand.

A VFD controls motor speed by varying the frequency of electrical power supplied to the motor. This allows compressor output to respond to changing air demand rather than relying exclusively on fixed-speed load/unload operation.

### Practical Benefits of VFD Operation

- Compressor output can be adjusted according to changing air demand within the permitted speed range.
- Variable-speed control can help maintain the required system pressure when correctly configured.
- Reduced unloading periods may improve energy performance in suitable demand profiles.
- Variable-speed operation can reduce unnecessary start-stop cycling.
- The compressor can support industrial systems with changing production loads.

### Energy Performance Considerations

- Operating pressure

- Operating hours and production shifts
- Motor and drive efficiency
- Compressor control settings
- Simultaneous operation of other compressors

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV120 uses rotary screw compression technology, in which two intermeshing helical rotors trap and progressively reduce the volume of air as it moves through the compression chamber.

The principal functional stages are:

**Air Intake:** Atmospheric air enters through the intake filtration arrangement, where airborne particles are reduced before entering the compression system.

**Compression:** The rotating screw elements progressively compress the incoming air and raise its pressure.

**Lubrication and Temperature Management:** In an oil-injected configuration, compressor oil supports lubrication, sealing and heat removal during compression.

**Air-Oil Separation:** The separation arrangement removes entrained oil from the compressed-air stream in an oil-injected configuration.

**Cooling and Discharge:** The compressed-air and lubrication systems are cooled according to the supplied package arrangement before air is delivered to the downstream system.

Rotary screw technology is commonly used in industrial installations requiring substantial compressed-air output and extended operating schedules. Actual operating suitability depends on the selected configuration, cooling conditions, maintenance programme and application duty.

The SJ RV120 uses a Variable Frequency Drive to regulate motor speed according to compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

In a variable-speed compressor, motor speed is adjusted by changing the electrical frequency supplied to the motor. This allows compressor output to respond to changing air consumption rather than relying exclusively on fixed-speed operation.

For larger industrial systems, demand can fluctuate as production lines start and stop, pneumatic tools operate intermittently, and different departments consume air at different rates.

The VFD arrangement can provide the following operational benefits when correctly selected and commissioned:

- Variable compressor output according to changing air demand.
- Reduced unnecessary full-speed operation during compatible partial-load conditions.
- More controlled pressure regulation within the configured operating range.
- Reduced frequency of conventional load/unload cycling in suitable applications.
- Controlled motor acceleration according to the drive configuration.
- Potential improvement in specific energy consumption under suitable variable-demand conditions.

## Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV150 uses rotary screw compression technology. A rotary screw airend compresses incoming air through the interaction of two rotating screw rotors housed inside a precision-machined casing.

The basic compression sequence involves:

**Air intake:** Atmospheric air enters through the compressor intake system.

**Air compression:** The rotating screw elements progressively reduce the volume of trapped air, increasing its pressure.

**Oil separation and cooling:** In an oil-injected configuration, lubricating oil supports sealing, cooling and lubrication during compression. The compressed air-oil mixture is subsequently processed through the separation system.

**Final air delivery:** Compressed air passes through the relevant internal and external treatment stages before entering the plant's distribution network.

The exact airend design, lubrication arrangement and internal component specification should be confirmed against the supplied machine configuration.

Rotary screw technology is widely used in industrial compressed-air installations because it supports continuous production requirements and centralised air distribution when correctly sized, installed and maintained.

## Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) Technology

The SJ RV150 uses variable frequency drive technology to regulate compressor motor speed according to compressed-air demand.

In a conventional fixed-speed installation, the motor operates at a fixed speed during loaded operation, with capacity generally controlled through load/unload operation. A VFD-based compressor can vary motor speed within its designed operating range to adjust air production.

### How VFD Control Works

1. The plant's compressed-air demand changes as connected equipment starts, stops or changes its operating cycle.
2. The compressor control system responds to the operating pressure and demand signal.
3. The VFD adjusts the motor's operating speed within the permitted range.
4. Compressor air delivery changes in response to the adjusted operating speed.
5. The system regulates output to maintain the required compressed-air supply within its control limits.

### Where Variable-Speed Operation Is Relevant

VFD operation can be useful in plants with:

- Multiple production shifts with different air consumption
- Intermittently operated pneumatic machinery
- Automated manufacturing lines with changing demand
- Production processes with varying operating cycles
- Central compressed-air networks serving different departments

### Energy Consumption Considerations

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of energy savings. Actual electrical consumption depends on the demand profile, operating pressure, compressor control range, leakage, motor and drive efficiency, and total operating hours.

For a meaningful energy comparison, the facility should evaluate specific power consumption:

**Specific power = Electrical input power (kW) ÷ Delivered airflow (m³/min)**

The comparison should use measured electrical input and actual delivered airflow at the same operating pressure and air-quality conditions. A VFD compressor operating continuously near its maximum capacity may offer limited energy advantage over an appropriately selected fixed-speed machine.

## Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV175 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. The compression process takes place inside a precision-machined airend containing two rotating screw elements.

### Compression Process

**1. Air intake:** Atmospheric air enters the compressor through the intake filtration arrangement.

**2. Air compression:** The rotating screw elements trap and progressively compress incoming air as the available volume between the rotors decreases.

**3. Lubrication and thermal management:** In an oil-injected configuration, lubricating oil supports sealing, cooling and lubrication during the compression process.

**4. Oil separation:** The compressed air-oil mixture passes through the separation arrangement in an oil-injected design, allowing separated oil to be returned to the lubrication circuit.

**5. Compressed-air delivery:** The compressed air proceeds through the relevant cooling and treatment stages before entering the downstream distribution system.

The precise airend construction, lubrication arrangement and internal component specifications should be confirmed against the supplied machine configuration.

### Engineering Considerations for High-Pressure Operation

At 13 bar, the compressor operates against a higher pressure ratio than it does at 8 bar. This affects the compression work, thermal loading and available airflow.

For this reason, the following parameters are important:

- Airend operating conditions
- Cooling system capacity
- Lubricant condition, where applicable
- Intake-air temperature
- Pressure-control settings
- Air-treatment equipment pressure drop
- Maintenance condition of filters and separators

A compressor's nominal motor horsepower alone does not establish its actual performance. Pressure-specific airflow is the more relevant reference when assessing the machine against a process requirement.

## Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) Technology

The SJ RV175 incorporates Variable Frequency Drive technology to adjust compressor motor speed in response to changing compressed-air demand.

In fixed-speed operation, the motor generally runs at a fixed speed during loaded operation, with compressor output managed through the applicable load/unload control arrangement. A VFD compressor can vary motor speed within its approved operating range to regulate air production.

### VFD Operating Principle

1. Compressed-air consumption changes as production equipment starts, stops or changes operating cycles.
2. The compressor control system monitors the relevant operating conditions, including system pressure where configured.
3. The VFD adjusts the electrical supply frequency to control motor speed.
4. The compressor's air delivery changes in response to the adjusted operating speed.
5. The control system regulates output within the machine's designed operating limits.

### Industrial Benefits of Variable-Speed Control

VFD operation can be relevant to large facilities with:

- Fluctuating compressed-air consumption across production shifts
- Intermittent operation of high-consumption machinery
- Multiple production departments with different demand patterns
- Automated manufacturing processes with changing air requirements
- Centralised compressed-air systems with variable loading

### Energy Consumption and Operating Economics

The economic benefit of a VFD compressor depends on the actual load profile. A plant with substantial periods of partial demand may have a different energy-consumption pattern from a plant operating continuously near full capacity.

The correct comparison requires measured electrical input and delivered airflow.

**Specific power consumption:**

Specific Power = Electrical Input Power (kW) ÷ Delivered Airflow (m³/min)

For a meaningful comparison, the fixed-speed and VFD alternatives should be assessed at equivalent operating pressure, air quality and production demand.

VFD technology does not guarantee a predetermined energy-saving percentage. Minimum speed limitations, control range, operating pressure, leakage, motor efficiency, drive losses and operating hours all influence the result.

## Advanced Rotary Screw Compression Technology

The SJ RV220 uses single-stage rotary screw compression technology. Rotary screw compressors operate through the interaction of two precision-machined helical rotors housed inside a compression element.

As air enters the compression element, it is trapped between the rotor profiles and casing. The rotation of the screw elements progressively reduces the trapped air volume, increasing its pressure before the compressed air moves towards the discharge side.

The rotary screw operating principle is suited to industrial compressed-air systems requiring substantial airflow and regular operation.

### Key Engineering Characteristics

**Continuous rotary compression principle**

The screw element produces compressed air through continuous rotor rotation rather than the reciprocating piston movement used in piston compressors.

**High-capacity airflow**

The SJ RV220 is specified for 740 CFM (20.95 m³/min) at 13 bar. This makes it relevant to large industrial systems where substantial airflow is required at elevated pressure.

**Single-stage compression configuration**

The model is identified as a single-stage rotary screw compressor. The specified pressure and airflow should be considered together when evaluating the complete system.

**Industrial compressed-air integration**

The compressor can be integrated with an appropriately rated air receiver, moisture separator, air dryer, filtration equipment and distribution network. Each downstream component must be selected for the actual operating pressure, airflow and required air quality.

**Operating-condition dependence**

Actual system performance and operating cost depend on inlet-air conditions, ambient temperature, cooling, pressure settings, maintenance condition, electrical supply and downstream pressure losses.

## Variable Frequency Drive (VFD/VSD) Technology

The SJ RV220 uses Variable Frequency Drive technology to regulate compressor motor speed according to changing compressed-air demand within its designed operating range.

In a conventional fixed-speed arrangement, the motor operates at a fixed speed during loaded operation, with capacity commonly managed through load/unload control. In a VFD-controlled arrangement, the drive varies motor speed to adjust compressor output as system demand changes.

### How VFD Control Works

1. Compressed-air demand changes across the connected production system.
2. The control system monitors operating conditions using the supplied control configuration.
3. The VFD adjusts the motor's operating speed within its permitted range.
4. Compressor output changes in response to the demand and pressure-control requirements.
5. When demand decreases, the compressor can reduce output rather than relying exclusively on repeated full-capacity loading and unloading.

### Operational Advantages

- **Variable airflow control:** Compressor output can respond to changing plant demand within the permitted operating range.
- **Pressure regulation:** Variable-speed operation can help maintain the configured system pressure as air consumption changes.
- **Part-load energy management:** Reducing motor speed during suitable partial-load conditions can reduce power consumption compared with operating continuously at full speed.
- **Reduced load/unload dependence:** VFD operation can reduce reliance on repeated full-capacity loading and unloading under suitable demand conditions.
- **Large-system adaptability:** Useful for industrial facilities where several production sections operate with different air-consumption patterns.

### Energy Consumption Considerations

VFD technology does not guarantee a fixed percentage of energy savings. Actual savings depend on the plant's demand profile, compressor operating range, pressure settings, leakage, operating hours, control strategy and comparison with the existing compressor arrangement.

For a 220 HP compressor, an energy assessment should compare measured electrical input (kW) against actual delivered airflow over representative operating periods. The most useful metric is specific power:

**Specific Power = Electrical Input (kW) ÷ Delivered Airflow (m³/min)**

A lower specific-power value indicates better electrical efficiency at the measured operating condition, provided the airflow and pressure measurement methods are comparable.

## Optional Features and System Configurations

The compressor can be evaluated as part of a complete compressed-air station. The following equipment may be specified separately according to the plant's airflow, pressure, air-quality and installation requirements.

**1. Air Receiver Tank**

An appropriately sized air receiver stores compressed air, helps manage short-duration demand fluctuations and supports stable system operation. The vessel must be rated for the system's maximum operating pressure and applicable statutory requirements.

**2. Refrigerated Air Dryer**

A refrigerated dryer removes moisture from compressed air to achieve a specified pressure dew point. Its rated capacity must be checked at the actual inlet pressure, temperature and ambient conditions.

**3. Desiccant Air Dryer**

A desiccant dryer may be selected where a lower pressure dew point is required, particularly for moisture-sensitive industrial processes. Purge-air consumption and regeneration energy should be included in operating-cost calculations.

**4. Moisture Separator**

A moisture separator removes bulk liquid condensate from compressed air before downstream treatment equipment.

**5. Pre-Filter and After-Filter**

Compressed-air filters remove specified levels of particulate contamination, water aerosols and oil aerosols, depending on filter grade and configuration.

**6. Micro Filter and Activated Carbon Filter**

Fine filtration and activated carbon treatment may be required for applications with more stringent oil-aerosol or vapour requirements. Filter selection must follow the actual compressed-air quality specification.

**7. Automatic Condensate Drain**

Automatic drains discharge collected condensate from receivers, separators, dryers and filters. Drain capacity and compatibility should be checked against the expected condensate load.

**8. Oil-Water Separator**

For oil-injected compressor systems, an oil-water separator may be required to treat condensate before disposal, subject to local environmental and discharge regulations.

**9. Compressed-Air Distribution Piping**

A suitably sized industrial piping network distributes compressed air while controlling pressure losses. Material selection, pressure rating, installation design and condensate management must be considered.

**10. Monitoring Instruments**

Airflow meters, pressure transmitters, pressure gauges and dew-point monitoring instruments can be added where the plant requires system-level performance measurement.

## Application Selection and Engineering Limitations

The SJ RV220 is a high-capacity, high-pressure compressor. Its 220 HP motor rating alone does not establish suitability for a particular plant.

Before finalizing the equipment, evaluate:

- **Total air consumption:** Calculate the actual simultaneous demand of all connected machines.
- **Required pressure:** Confirm the minimum pressure required at the equipment inlet, including distribution and treatment losses.
- **Demand variation:** Assess whether the plant's load profile is suitable for variable-speed compressor operation.
- **Air quality:** Establish the required particulate, moisture and oil-content limits.
- **System pressure rating:** Verify every pressure-containing component against the maximum intended system pressure.
- **Operating environment:** Account for ambient temperature, dust, ventilation and altitude where relevant.
- **Electrical infrastructure:** Confirm available electrical capacity and compatibility with the 160 kW motor and VFD arrangement.

A compressor rated at 740 CFM does not necessarily deliver 740 CFM at every downstream machine. Air-treatment equipment, piping, filters, regulators, valves and other restrictions create pressure losses that must be included in system design.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### 1. What is the air delivery of the SJ RV220 220 HP compressor at 13 bar?

The SJ RV220 is specified to deliver 740 CFM (20.95 m³/min) at 13 bar (190 PSI).

### 2. What is the motor power of the SJ RV220?

The compressor has a rated motor power of 220 HP, equivalent to 160 kW.

### 3. What is the difference between the SJ RV220 VFD and a fixed-speed 220 HP compressor?

The VFD version varies motor speed within its designed operating range to adjust compressor output according to changing air demand. A fixed-speed compressor operates at a fixed motor speed during loaded operation and commonly manages demand through load/unload control.

### 4. Can the SJ RV220 operate continuously in a large industrial plant?

Its suitability for the intended operating duty must be confirmed against the manufacturer's approved duty, operating limits, cooling requirements and maintenance schedule. Continuous operation should not be assumed solely from the 220 HP rating.

### 5. Is 13 bar suitable for mining and DTH drilling?

It may be suitable where the drilling equipment manufacturer specifies compatible operating pressure and the required airflow is within the compressor's delivery capability. Actual rig demand, hose losses and operating conditions must be checked.

### 6. Can the SJ RV220 be used for abrasive blasting?

It can be evaluated for large abrasive-blasting systems if the total simultaneous nozzle airflow requirement is within its specified capacity. Nozzle size, blasting pressure, moisture control and filtration must be considered.

### 7. Does a VFD compressor always reduce electricity consumption?

No. Savings depend on the actual load profile, operating range, pressure settings, leakage, operating hours and control strategy. Energy performance should be assessed through measured electrical input and delivered airflow.

### 8. What size air receiver tank is required for the SJ RV220?

There is no universally correct receiver volume based only on compressor horsepower. Sizing depends on demand fluctuations, control response, permissible pressure variation, required reserve capacity and system design.

### 9. Which air dryer is suitable for a 220 HP, 13 bar compressor?

The dryer must be selected for the actual airflow and corrected operating conditions, including inlet pressure, inlet temperature and ambient temperature. A refrigerated dryer may be sufficient for general industrial air, while a desiccant dryer may be needed for lower pressure dew points.

### 10. Can the compressor supply multiple production lines?

Yes, provided the combined simultaneous airflow demand, pressure requirements and air-quality requirements are within the designed system capacity. The distribution network must be sized to control pressure drop and leakage.

### 11. Can the SJ RV220 supply 8 bar, 10 bar and 13 bar systems?

The official specification sheet lists separate airflow ratings at all three pressure points: 1,035 CFM at 8 bar, 930 CFM at 10 bar and 740 CFM at 13 bar. The actual operating pressure and control range must follow the approved machine configuration.

### 12. What should be checked before installing a 220 HP VFD compressor?

Check the plant's measured airflow demand, required operating pressure, electrical supply, ventilation, foundation and access, air-treatment requirements, receiver sizing, piping pressure rating and maintenance provisions.
